Exploiting government property to burnish celebrity and glamorize politicians goes against American traditions that require equality for all over the enhancement of status for a favored few, says Cato’s Dan Greenberg.

If states can label private continuing education “government speech,” they can sidestep the First Amendment and mandate ideological content across medicine, law, counseling, and more. Cato urges the Supreme Court to draw the line in Khatibi v. Lawson.

The Trump–Xi summit revealed a hard truth: years of US tariffs did not force China’s economic retreat. Beijing adapted by diversifying trade, expanding exports elsewhere, and exploiting US policy mistakes. Meanwhile, chaotic tariffs and the Iran war weakened Washington’s leverage while raising costs at home, explains Cato's @scottlincicome.

ow.ly/APOc50Z4Vjf

When states spend federal taxpayer dollars on welfare programs they administer, we shouldn’t be surprised when billions are lost due to improper payments. Congress should require all welfare payments to be screened through Treasury’s “Do Not Pay” system, which verifies eligibility in real time.

Social Security’s long-term shortfall is likely significantly worse than projected. 
 
The Trustees' projections rely on fertility assumptions far more optimistic than those of the CBO or the Census Bureau. Use more realistic numbers, and Social Security’s 75-year deficit rises to at least $30 trillion. Learn more from Cato’s Romina Boccia and Krit Chanwong.

Cato’s Nicholas Anthony testified on the Hill last week, explaining that the Bank Secrecy Act forces banks to file 28.7 million reports on customers yearly, yet the IRS opens just 275 criminal cases from them. It’s time to stop treating bank customers as guilty until proven innocent.

Since 1980, a majority of all legal immigrants — 56% — received permanent residence by adjusting status once inside the United States. 
  
With USCIS’s new policy, however, the majority of the 1.2 million backlogged legal immigrants with pending green card applications for legal permanent residence will have to self-deport, explains Cato’s @David_J_Bier.
